title: Use AI, but don’t mask it
content_html:
• CORRESPONDENCE
  • 28 July 2026

By

  • Francesco Branda0
  1. Francesco Branda

    1. Campus Bio-Medico University of Rome, Rome, Italy.

The rise of artificial-intelligence ‘humanizer’ tools (see Nature 655, 556–557; 2026) presents science with a philosophical puzzle dressed as a technological one. These tools, designed to strip away the sterile fingerprints of machine-generated prose, promise to restore a personal voice to academic writing. Yet in pursuing authenticity, they might inadvertently erode the very foundation of scholarly trust.
